blocks.text: Say your strongest story out loud in five beats with a timer. Aim for about two minutes, then note where you ran long.
Tell the same story again, adding one sentence each for scope, ownership, judgment, collaboration, and growth.

days.title: Friction
days.blurb: A disagreement, then a mistake. Both told with you as the subject.

blocks.text: Out loud: state the other person's position in a real disagreement the way they would state it. Then tell the full story.
Out loud: tell one real mistake, saying the mistake in your first sentence. Keep the damage to about a fifth of the answer.

days.title: Reach
days.blurb: Fog into a plan, and a yes from someone who does not report to you.

blocks.text: Out loud: tell an ambiguity story and name the exact moment the problem got edges, and what you wrote down.

days.title: Depth
days.blurb: Three zoom levels on one project, then a deadline you bent.

blocks.text: Give your project's thirty-second headline, stop, then give the five-minute walkthrough with the diagram and three real numbers.
Out loud: tell a deadline story that names the cut, the reason, and the person you warned, and when.

days.title: Close
days.blurb: Questions that surface how the team works, then one story bent three ways.

blocks.text: Ask your six prepared closing questions out loud, and add one follow-up to each as if you had heard an answer.
Answer three prompts out loud with the same story: a project you are proud of, a disagreement, a mistake. Pull a different beat forward each time.
Re-tell yesterday's deadline story from memory in under two minutes without notes.

days.title: Story mix
days.blurb: One sitting. Unlabeled behavioral prompts, answered aloud.

blocks.text: Have a friend or a random timer pick one of the five topics. Start answering out loud within ten seconds, then note which scoring signals you left empty.
Do the thirty-second headline, the five-minute walkthrough, and a one-box deep dive on your project back to back, out loud, without notes.
